"Perhaps in Johor, God willing, with the economic resources we have, we can continue upgrading our stadiums. But for the rest of the country, I don't think we're there yet. In Malaysia, I can only say: forget about it.

Forget it. Why do I say that?

Because even after 13 years of telling them to replace the grass, the pitch still hasn't been changed. Yet they can dream about becoming... about hosting the World Cup.

It's better to forget about it.

What puzzles me is that the states refusing to replace their pitches aren't poor states. They're wealthy states. Yet the pitches are still like cow pasture, the stadiums are still in poor condition, and nobody questions it. Instead, people are more interested in questioning Johor or trying to link everything back to me.

Well, I suppose they're jealous of what we've achieved over the past 13 years.

That's what's happening. So if Malaysia wants to host the World Cup, it's better not to bother."

🗣️ Tunku Ismail Sultan Ibrahim, Regent of Johor and owner of Johor Darul Ta'zim reply about question "Qatar, which is 29 times smaller than Malaysia can be host the 2022 World Cup, Can our country, or Johor, organize it?" on the Bual Santai Petang Bersama Orang Muda podcast on 20 June 2026 at the Tunku Mahkota Ismail Youth Centre (TMIYC), Muar
